jurisdiction.name: Pakistan
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Pakistan governs AI through policy rather than AI-specific law: the National AI Policy approved in July 2025 (replacing a 2022 draft) and the February 2026 Islamabad AI Declaration set the direction, and the Digital Nation Pakistan Act 2025 gives the Pakistan Digital Authority powers over AI oversight and standards. The national judicial policy-making committee issued guidelines on AI use in courts in April 2026 and the national CERT advised on safe use of generative AI. A 2026 data governance policy with rules on automated decision systems in government and a personal data protection bill with automated-decision rights are still drafts.
lead_institutions: Ministry of Information Technology and Telecommunication
narrative.review_notes: This review was completed on 12 October 2026 and covers national law, government, ministries and regulators. Not yet verified from the official text: AI guidance from the central bank, the securities regulator and the higher education commission, which is listed as leads.

instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Information Technology and Telecommunication
instruments.publisher_name: Ministry of Information Technology and Telecommunication
instruments.current_status: Listed as 'Approved' with approval date 31 July 2025 in the Ministry of IT & Telecom's official Policies register; the PDF calls itself the National Artificial Intelligence Policy – 2025. It replaces the 2022/2023 consultation draft (also still listed in the register as 'Draft'). A policy, not a statute: the AI Council, AI Directorate and National AI Fund it proposes have no legislative basis in the document.
instruments.summary: Pakistan's national AI policy, built on four pillars: an AI innovation ecosystem (National AI Fund, Centres of Excellence in AI, venture and innovation funds, data standards), awareness and readiness (national awareness programme, upskilling, public-servant training), a secure AI ecosystem (transparency and human oversight, a public register of public-sector AI systems, data security, generative-AI guidance by a proposed AI Directorate, AI regulatory sandboxes) and transformation and evolution (sector roadmaps, international alignment). It sets up an AI Council chaired by the Federal Minister for IT and Telecom as the apex oversight body, with a Policy Implementation Cell in MoITT, and sets KPIs such as at least 50 enterprises in AI regulatory sandboxes by 2027.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Pakistan's adopted national AI strategy and the anchor for its AI governance institutions (AI Council, AI Directorate, CoE-AI).
instruments.evidence_reference: curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60): full 28-page PDF read (pdftotext); 'Approved, 31 July, 2025' read on the ministry's Policies register (https://www.moitt.gov.pk/Policies)

instruments.summary: Consultation draft of Pakistan's first national AI policy, prepared by MoITT with consultants. It proposed an AI Regulatory Directorate, a National AI Fund, Centres of Excellence in AI, a national high-tech curriculum and sector adoption roadmaps, with time-bound targets mostly set for 2023. It was replaced by the 2025 policy.

instruments.official_title: Islamabad AI Declaration on Sovereign, Responsible, and Capability-Driven Artificial Intelligence
instruments.english_title: Islamabad AI Declaration on Sovereign, Responsible, and Capability-Driven Artificial Intelligence
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Information Technology and Telecommunication
instruments.publisher_name: Ministry of Information Technology and Telecommunication
instruments.current_status: Published on the Ministry of IT & Telecom website ('AI Declaration' page) dated Islamabad, 9 February 2026. A political declaration of principles; no legal effect is stated.
instruments.summary: Government declaration setting nine principles for Pakistan's approach to AI: sovereign purpose and public value, human accountability for decisions of public consequence, a use-case-first approach, sovereign data stewardship, explainable, auditable and risk-proportionate AI in government, coordinated whole-of-government oversight, capability and inclusion, a private-sector-led AI economy with sovereign compute, and responsible AI diplomacy. It frames AI as private-sector led and government enabled.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Current high-level statement of AI governance principles, including explainability and human oversight for government AI.
instruments.evidence_reference: curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60): full text of the declaration read on the MoITT page

instruments.english_title: Data Governance Policy 2026 (National Data Governance Policy, DNP-D.001 POL) - draft
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Information Technology and Telecommunication; Pakistan Digital Authority (publishing authority named in the document)
instruments.publisher_name: Ministry of Information Technology and Telecommunication
instruments.current_status: Listed as 'Draft' with date 26 June 2026 in the ministry's Policies register; the document (dated June 2026, version 1.1, maturity 'PROPOSED') states that it takes effect on formal issuance by the Pakistan Digital Authority after Cabinet approval and Gazette notification, which were pending.
instruments.summary: Draft national policy for governance of public-sector data held by federal public bodies and their contractors, issued under the Digital Nation Pakistan Act, 2025. Its clause 14 sets a risk-tiered approach to AI and automated decision-making in government: pre-production registration, model accountability, explainability and drift monitoring for high-risk uses, meaningful human review and redress for automated decisions with legal effects, a public registry of automated decision systems kept by the Pakistan Digital Authority, data-governance and ethics requirements in AI procurement, and controls on public bodies' use of generative AI.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Would set the first rules on government AI and automated decision-making, including an algorithmic transparency register.
instruments.evidence_reference: curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60): full PDF read (pdftotext), incl. clause 14 and Annex III; register entry 'Data Governance Policy 2026, Draft, IT, 26 June, 2026' on https://www.moitt.gov.pk/Policies

instruments.official_title: Draft of the Personal Data Protection Bill, 2023
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Information Technology and Telecommunication
instruments.publisher_name: Ministry of Information Technology and Telecommunication
instruments.current_status: Listed as 'Personal Data Protection Bill May 2023 - Draft' (status Draft, date 1 May 2023) on the ministry's Legislation page, alongside earlier 2018 and 2020 drafts. No enacted federal personal data protection law was found on official portals as of 12 October 2026; Pakistan has no data protection authority yet.
instruments.summary: Final draft of a federal personal data protection bill that would set lawful grounds for processing, data-subject rights and a National Commission for Personal Data Protection as regulator. Section 29 gives data subjects the right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing, including profiling, that produces legal obligations or significant harm unless they gave explicit consent, and a right to information about automated decision-making and to human intervention (with a public-interest exception).
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Would introduce Pakistan's first automated-decision-making and profiling safeguards.
instruments.evidence_reference: curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60): full PDF read (pdftotext), incl. s.29; register entry on https://moitt.gov.pk/Legislations

instruments.official_title: National Guidelines for Use of Artificial Intelligence in Judicial Institutions of Pakistan
instruments.english_title: National Guidelines for Use of Artificial Intelligence in Judicial Institutions of Pakistan
instruments.publisher_name: Law and Justice Commission of Pakistan (Secretariat of the NJPMC)
instruments.current_status: Approved by the NJPMC at its 57th meeting and announced on 29 April 2026 (LJCP announcement page, which links the full text). Clause 1 states the Guidelines 'shall come into force at once'; they are to be followed by the superior and subordinate courts, tribunals, special courts and other justice-sector institutions, and their implementation is subject to laws in force and High Courts' autonomy.
instruments.summary: Guidelines from Pakistan's apex judicial policy committee for the use of AI systems in courts and other justice-sector institutions, aligned with the National AI Policy 2025. They require human-in-the-loop use in which judges record independent reasoning, disclosure with references of AI-generated portions of documents and how they were verified, compliance with data protection rules and training for judges and staff. They list permitted uses (case management, legal research, predictive analytics for case duration and patterns, summaries and draft texts) and prefer locally developed explainable AI trained on Pakistani legal data.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: First AI-specific rules for the judiciary in Pakistan.
instruments.evidence_reference: curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60): LJCP announcement page (29 April 2026, 57th NJPMC meeting) read; the LJCP PDF is image-only, so the full text was read from the identical copy published by the Balochistan High Court (https://bhc.gov.pk/media/downloads/95.pdf) via pdftotext

instruments.official_title: National CERT Advisory: Safe and Secure Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) Tools and Platforms
instruments.english_title: National CERT Advisory No. 18 (NCA-18.011026): Safe and Secure Use of Generative AI Tools and Platforms
instruments.issuing_authority: National Cyber Emergency Response Team of Pakistan
instruments.publisher_name: National Cyber Emergency Response Team of Pakistan
instruments.current_status: Advisory No. 18 of 2026 in PKCERT's official advisories list. It is phrased as 'mandatory security and governance measures' that organizations 'are advised' to implement, but no statutory basis is cited, so it is recorded as guidance.
instruments.summary: National CERT advisory on 'Shadow AI' and the security risks of public AI chatbots, coding assistants, extensions and third-party AI services. It advises organizations to enforce a generative-AI acceptable use policy, bar classified, personal or proprietary data from public or unapproved AI tools, keep a vetted registry of approved AI tools, require human review of AI-generated code and critical outputs, extend DLP and monitoring to AI interfaces, align with the NIST AI RMF and OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications, train staff and keep audit trails of AI use.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: National cyber authority's security guidance on generative AI use.
instruments.evidence_reference: curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60): full PDF read (pdftotext); listed as Advisory No 18 of 2026 on https://pkcert.gov.pk/advisories.asp; date from reference NCA-18.011026 and PDF metadata (1 Oct 2026) Status note: Publication date reduced from 2026-10-01 to 2026 (date audit 2026-10-13): Only the reference number 'NCA-18.011026' encodes a date; no date is printed in the advisory, so only the year is kept (decoding a reference number is not a stated date).

instruments.english_title: Digital Nation Pakistan Act, 2025 (Act No. I of 2025)
instruments.current_status: Act No. I of 2025; received Presidential assent and published in the Gazette of Pakistan (Extraordinary, Part I) on 29 January 2025; s.1(3): comes into force at once. In force. Not an AI-specific law; recorded for its explicit AI provision (s.8(g)).
instruments.summary: Federal law establishing the National Digital Commission (chaired by the Prime Minister) and the Pakistan Digital Authority to drive Pakistan's digital transformation under a National Digital Masterplan. Section 8(g) empowers the Pakistan Digital Authority to carry out oversight, set standards, enforce compliance and establish frameworks in areas assigned by the Commission, expressly including data management and governance and artificial intelligence, without overlapping other regulators; s.8(h) tasks it with a National Data Strategy and data-governance framework.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Statutory basis for the Pakistan Digital Authority's AI oversight and standard-setting role (used for the draft Data Governance Policy 2026).
instruments.evidence_reference: curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60): full Gazette text read (pdftotext) from the National Assembly site Published in: Senate Secretariat (Gazette of Pakistan, Extraordinary).

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: Pakistan's national law and gazette sources, the IT and telecoms ministry, the judiciary, other ministries and regulators were searched, and no qualifying AI-governance document was found for standards, readiness indices or international agreements. Some official sites, including those of the State Bank of Pakistan, the securities regulator and the Higher Education Commission, were unavailable, and the national law database search did not work. Documents reported on those sites, such as the central bank's AI guidelines and the higher-education AI framework, are listed as leads to check later.
coverage_audit.technical_note:
Coverage note (original): Technical review notes: tier B/C batch run 2026-10-12, one agent, national level only (PROTOCOL §6), about 25-minute time box. sbp.org.pk and secp.gov.pk 403 to curl and WebFetch; hec.gov.pk reset/503; pakistancode.gov.pk search errors. PECA (Amendment) Act 2025 read in full: no AI/deepfake wording, not recorded. Judicial guidelines read from the identical Balochistan High Court copy (LJCP copy image-only). Data Governance Policy kept as draft (ministry list still says Draft). Not a party to Convention 108. Units covered: Law: Gazette texts on na.gov.pk read: Digital Nation Pakistan Act 2025 (s.8(g) AI oversight power, recorded) and Prevention of Electronic Crimes (Amendment) Act 2025 (Act II of 2025; fake/false information offence s.26A and Social Media Protection and Regulatory Authority; read in full, contains no AI, deepfake or synthetic-media wording, so not recorded as an AI instrument). Senate bill tracker: Regulation of Artificial Intelligence Bill 2024 withdrawn from committee (lead). No enacted AI-specific law and no enacted personal data protection law found. pakistancode.gov.pk search pages returned errors.; Government: MoITT Policies and Legislations registers and AI Declaration page fully reviewed: National AI Policy 2025 (approved 31 Jul 2025), 2022 consultation draft (superseded), Islamabad AI Declaration (9 Feb 2026), draft Data Governance Policy 2026, draft Personal Data Protection Bill 2023 recorded. Digital Pakistan Policy 2018 has a short AI/IoT/FinTech innovation-centre clause only (not recorded as an AI strategy). Searched for a PDA 'AI Supervisory Framework': nothing official found.; Ministries: Judiciary: NJPMC National Guidelines for Use of AI in Judicial Institutions (recorded). Education: HEC Framework on use of GenAI tools in HEIs exists on hec.gov.pk but the site was unreachable (lead). National CERT (under MoITT): GenAI advisory recorded; National Cybersecurity Handbook 2026-27 is a general cyber handbook (image-only PDF) with AI-use rules for officials, not recorded as an AI instrument. No AI-specific documents found for health, defence, finance/FBR, labour or interior.; Regulators: No data protection authority exists (PDP Bill still draft). State Bank of Pakistan: site returned 403 to curl and WebFetch; reported AI guidelines not located (lead). SECP: sandbox guidelines (2019, AI as one eligible category, not AI-specific) page returned 403 to curl and WebFetch. PTA: no AI-specific instrument found. Convention 108: Pakistan is not a party. Standards: no PSQCA adoption of AI standards (ISO/IEC 42001, 22989) found - searched, nothing found. Index/readiness: no government-published AI index or maturity assessment found - searched, nothing found. International: no AI treaty signed or ratified found (bilateral AI cooperation with Saudi Arabia reported in news only) - searched, nothing found.. Not reached: State Bank of Pakistan website (sbp.org.pk, HTTP 403 to curl and WebFetch); SECP website (secp.gov.pk, HTTP 403 to curl and WebFetch); Higher Education Commission website (hec.gov.pk, connection reset / HTTP 503); pakistancode.gov.pk search. Could not verify: SBP AI guidelines (site 403); SECP AI-related sandbox/guidance (site 403); HEC GenAI framework (site unreachable); PDA national AI Supervisory Framework (no official document found). standards, index-readiness, international: no material found.
Wording note 2026-10-19 (narrative.review_notes): The central bank, securities regulator and higher education commission websites could not be reached, so their AI guidance is listed as leads.
